WITH order_invoice_counts AS (
  SELECT o.order_id, COUNT(i.invoice_number) AS invoice_count
  FROM Orders AS o
  LEFT JOIN Invoices AS i ON i.order_id = o.order_id
  GROUP BY o.order_id
), totals AS (
  SELECT SUM(invoice_count) AS total_invoice_count
  FROM order_invoice_counts
), overall AS (
  SELECT AVG(1.0 * c.invoice_count / NULLIF(t.total_invoice_count, 0)) AS average_share,
         t.total_invoice_count
  FROM order_invoice_counts AS c
  CROSS JOIN totals AS t
  GROUP BY t.total_invoice_count
)
SELECT SUM(c.invoice_count) AS total_invoices,
       AVG(1.0 * c.invoice_count / o.total_invoice_count) AS average_share,
       AVG(1.0 * c.invoice_count / o.total_invoice_count - o.average_share) AS average_excess_share
FROM order_invoice_counts AS c
CROSS JOIN overall AS o
WHERE 1.0 * c.invoice_count / o.total_invoice_count > o.average_share;

assumptions.assumption: At least one invoice exists overall, so the total invoice count used as the share denominator is nonzero.
